evidence.origin: temp/ux_matrix/ evidence store, scored 2026-10-26, re-verified + SC-C2 rescored 2026-10-27

live_recompute.note: This is the live run from evidence_current.json against run.py. It is the machine-verifiable form of the current score.

current_rating_proof.derived_from: mean of mapped scenario dimensions SC-A1, SC-A2, SC-A3, SC-B1, SC-C1, SC-C2, SC-C3, SC-D1, SC-H1, SC-H3, SC-G1, SC-J2 (x20 scale, per score_evidence_20261029.json scenario_dimension_map)
current_rating_proof.anchor_meaning: 75 anchor = 'Core flows meet accessibility expectations'. Current 62 is below that anchor.
current_rating_proof.why_low: SC-H3 (high contrast) is scored 1.0 and pulls the accessibility mean down; the other accessibility-mapped scenarios are mid-to-high. The track gap analysis is consistent with this: core flows work, finer inclusive-interaction details need polish.

gap_between_baseline_and_current.note: Accessibility barely moved (60 to 62). The quick-wins landings that moved the matrix were mostly sidebar_control_quality, layer_visibility, and ai_arrange; accessibility was not a primary beneficiary.

evidence.important_caveat: This evidence is an AUTOMATED derivation from an e2e scenario matrix scaled x20 onto the 1-100 anchored matrix. It is NOT a human usability study (none exists on this tree) and it does NOT measure the matrix's zero-click gate on 10 representative sheets. The score_run_20261029.json disposition records this explicitly. A fresh session inherits the number as the current best evidence, not as a vetted usability-study score.
